# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 74

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 11

---

## Disagreement 1 — "in the form of the church" vs. "as the church"

- **EMET:** "in the form of the church"
- **LOGOS:** "in the form of the church"
- **PNEUMA:** "in the form of the church"
- **Greek:** *en tō schēmati tēs ekklēsias* — "in the form/appearance of the church"
- **Ruling:** All agents agree. No ruling needed.

---

## Disagreement 2 — "feeble in the flesh" vs. "weak in the flesh"

- **EMET:** "you are feeble in the flesh"
- **LOGOS:** "you were weak in the flesh"
- **PNEUMA:** "you were weak in the flesh"
- **Greek:** *asthenēs ēs tē sarki* — "you were weak in the flesh"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "you were weak in the flesh" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). The past tense is correct (*ēs* = imperfect "you were"); "weak" is the standard rendering of *asthenēs*.

---

## Disagreement 3 — "Speak with the Power" — all agree

- **EMET:** "Speak with the Power and it will come to you clearly"
- **LOGOS:** "Speak with the Power and it will come to you more clearly"
- **PNEUMA:** "Speak with the Power and it will all become clear"
- **Greek:** *lala meta tēs Dynameōs* — "speak with the Power"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "Speak with the Power and it will come to you more clearly" (LOGOS). The comparative *saphesteron* ("more clearly") should be preserved; PNEUMA loses the comparative force.

---

## Disagreement 4 — "led me away to" vs. "led me to" Arcadia

- **EMET:** "led me to Arcadia"
- **LOGOS:** "led me away to Arcadia"
- **PNEUMA:** "led me to Arcadia"
- **Greek:** *apēgagen me eis tēn Arkadian* — "led me away to Arcadia"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "led me to Arcadia" (EMET/PNEUMA). "Away" is implied in *apagō* but adds awkwardness in English without improving the meaning.

---

## Disagreement 5 — "black rocks" vs. "all black rock"

- **EMET:** "had black rocks"
- **LOGOS:** "was all black rock"
- **PNEUMA:** "covered with black rocks"
- **Greek:** *petras melainēs* — "of black rock/stones"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "was all black rock" (LOGOS). The genitive implies the mountain's substance; "all black rock" conveys this wholeness.

---

## Disagreement 6 — "half-withered" vs. "half dead"

- **EMET:** "vegetation that was half-withered"
- **LOGOS:** "vegetation that was half-withered"
- **PNEUMA:** "vegetation that was half dead"
- **Greek:** *hēmixēros* — "half-dry/half-withered"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "vegetation that was half-withered" (EMET/LOGOS). "Half-withered" is a direct rendering of *hēmixēros* ("half-dry"); "half dead" is interpretive.

---

## Disagreement 7 — "smiling vegetation" vs. "cheerful vegetation" vs. "lush and bright"

- **EMET:** "smiling vegetation"
- **LOGOS:** "cheerful vegetation"
- **PNEUMA:** "lush and bright — the whole thing was in full bloom"
- **Greek:** *hilaros* — "cheerful, joyful, merry"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "cheerful vegetation" (LOGOS). *Hilaros* means "cheerful/radiant/joyful" — "cheerful" is the precise English rendering; "smiling" is a metaphor; PNEUMA's "lush and bright" substitutes physical description for the Greek's affective quality.

---

## Disagreement 8 — "flourished and abounded" vs. "flourished"

- **EMET:** "the vegetation flourished"
- **LOGOS:** "the vegetation flourished and abounded"
- **PNEUMA:** "the vegetation grew and multiplied"
- **Greek:** *epleonaze kai exethallen hē chlōe* — "the vegetation abounded and flourished"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the vegetation flourished and abounded" (LOGOS). The two verbs *pleonazō* and *ekthalleō* should both be rendered; EMET omits one.

---

## Disagreement 9 — "ruminating" vs. "chewing their cud"

- **EMET:** "chewing their cud"
- **LOGOS:** "ruminating"
- **PNEUMA:** "chewing their cud"
- **Greek:** *mēryōmenoi* — "ruminating / chewing the cud"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "ruminating" (LOGOS). "Ruminating" is the precise technical term for the biological process; "chewing their cud" is accurate but more colloquial.

---

## Disagreement 10 — "densely covered" vs. "covered" with trees

- **EMET:** "covered with trees"
- **LOGOS:** "covered densely with trees"
- **PNEUMA:** "thickly forested"
- **Greek:** *katadendros holē* — "entirely tree-covered / densely wooded"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "densely covered with trees" (LOGOS). *Katadendros* means "thoroughly covered with trees" — "densely" captures the *kata-* prefix of thoroughness.

---

## Disagreement 11 — "radiant and joyful" vs. "cheerful" for the twelfth mountain

- **EMET:** "its appearance was cheerful"
- **LOGOS:** "its appearance was radiant and joyful"
- **PNEUMA:** "radiant and joyful to look at"
- **Greek:** *hilaros* — "cheerful/radiant/joyful"
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "its appearance was radiant and joyful" (LOGOS). For the twelfth mountain — the culminating, white mountain — the fuller rendering of *hilaros* as "radiant and joyful" is appropriate; the white (*leukos*) and cheerful (*hilaros*) together suggest a mountain of glory.

---

*Disagreement log generated 2026-03-17. SOPHIA rulings are binding for the consensus text.*
